uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. It is the number the Bank of England's 2% target is set against, and it moves gilt yields, sterling and mortgage pricing.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics reports how fast UK consumer prices rose over the year to September. The release settles whether price growth sped up or slowed in the month, and which goods and services drove the change.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target for overnight lending between US banks. Its decisions set the price of dollar credit, from American mortgages to debt owed abroad.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him over the renovation, so the committee sets rates with its chair under open pressure from the president. The argument in front of it has turned toward raising rates rather than cutting them, and this meeting is a test of whether it sets policy on prices alone.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for the countries that share the euro, meeting eight times a year. Its deposit rate anchors borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The decision comes with tightening in the air elsewhere: the Bank of Japan raised its rate to a 31-year high and traders have priced in Fed hikes. The ECB's own recent news from Frankfurt was about stablecoin yields and tokenized bonds, not rates, so this meeting is where it answers the same question for its own borrowers.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, Japanese government bond yields and the cost of funding trades worldwide borrowed in yen.
boj-2026-10.recent: The last meeting's hike was meant to curb rising prices, and the yen fell anyway: the dollar jumped above 157 yen after the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. This meeting settles whether the Bank tightens again into a weak currency, as its balancing act with Bessent over the yen gets harder.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. That rate feeds through to UK mortgages, business loans and savings, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee meets after the Bank of Japan raised its rate to a 31-year high and with Brent near $106 a barrel, an oil shock that lifts prices while it slows growth. The decision settles whether the Bank of England treats that squeeze as inflation to be fought or a hit to demand to be looked through.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. Its decisions move borrowing costs across the US economy and, through the dollar, in much of the rest of the world.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him, and the committee meets with that demand still standing. Traders have turned to pricing 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, so the decision settles whether the committee tightens while its chair is under direct attack from the president.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from the world's largest economies, hosted by a rotating presidency that sets the agenda. It makes no binding law; its weight is in who attends and what they agree to say together.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio invited Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to Miami, and the Kremlin is considering it. That puts the guest list, not the agenda, at the centre of a meeting the US hosts. It follows a Trump-Xi summit that Washington approached by capping Nvidia's compute sales to China.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets about every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs across the bloc, and the euro's exchange rate moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The decision comes with other central banks tightening: Japan raised its rate to a 31-year high and global government bond yields are near their highest since 2007. The ECB's own recent moves have been on stablecoin yields and tokenized bonds, not rates, so this meeting settles whether Frankfurt follows that turn or holds apart from it.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision feeds through to UK mortgage, loan and savings rates, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: Brent near $106 a barrel puts the committee between an imported price shock it cannot reach and borrowing costs that bond markets have already pushed to their highest since 2007. The Bank of Japan answered the same squeeze by raising rates; this meeting settles whether the Bank of England treats the oil price as a one-off.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board, which meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, the cost of Japan's vast government debt, and the flow of Japanese savings invested abroad.
boj-2026-12.recent: The last hike, made to curb rising prices, bought the yen no relief: the dollar jumped above 157 yen, and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. This meeting settles whether the Bank tightens again into a weak currency, while its balancing act with Bessent over the dollar and the yen gets harder.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly count of US payrolls, unemployment and wages, usually out on the first Friday. It is the labour-market reading the Federal Reserve steers by, and bonds, the dollar and gold move on it.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.recent: Gold slipped ahead of the release and is on course for a second weekly loss. The report settles how many jobs the US economy added last month, the figure that gold and other assets are repriced against.
